answer: An identity imprinting mechanism blocks sybil attacks by making each agent earn trust pigment over a long horizon of verifiable economic actions, not inheriting it. Every micro-task, honest transfer, and resolved dispute leaves faint cryptographic pigment in the agent ledger — a trail clones cannot share. Attackers must simulate months of genuine commerce per fake agent, because the scoring horizon is long enough that fake activity stands out like dead calm amid a zephyr of real organic exchange. Cost scales linearly, turning cheap sybil floods into astronomically expensive coordination work.
